analysis.summary: Spain, the reigning European champions and one of the tournament co-favorites, enter this Round of 32 clash as heavy favorites after topping Group H without conceding a single goal across three matches. Austria, guided by Ralf Rangnick's high-intensity pressing system, qualified from Group J in second place despite a rocky campaign that included a 0-2 defeat to Argentina. The talent gap is significant, but Austria's willingness to press aggressively and score in all three group games gives them a slim path if Spain's attack — already weakened by the confirmed absences of Nico Williams and Yeremy Pino — misfires.
analysis.home_form: Spain drew 0-0 with Cape Verde (wc-012), beat Saudi Arabia 4-0 (wc-036), and beat Uruguay 1-0 (wc-063) to top Group H with 7 points. Their defense has not conceded in 430 minutes of World Cup football. In possession Spain averaged approximately 74% against Cape Verde and 65% against Uruguay, accumulating around 11 corners per game. Key attackers Lamine Yamal and Mikel Oyarzabal are available; Rodri, Pedri, Fabian Ruiz and Merino anchor the midfield.
analysis.away_form: Austria beat Jordan 3-1 (wc-019), lost 0-2 to Argentina (wc-040), and drew 3-3 with Algeria (wc-071) to finish second in Group J on 4 points. They scored in all three group games but also conceded in all three, highlighting an attacking threat alongside defensive vulnerability. Rangnick's 4-2-3-1 with aggressive pressing was effective against lesser opposition but was nullified by Argentina.
analysis.h2h: Spain lead the all-time head-to-head record with 10 wins from 16 meetings (Austria 4 wins, 2 draws). Spain are unbeaten in the last five encounters (4W 1D). Spain's most emphatic win was a 9-0 in a Euro 2000 qualifier in 1999; the last meeting, an international friendly in 2009, ended 5-1 to Spain. Austria's only victory over Spain in a World Cup came at the 1978 tournament (2-1).
injuries_news: Nico Williams (adductor, right) — confirmed out for this match after limping off vs Uruguay; will remain in squad for potential later rounds.
Yeremy Pino (acromioclavicular sprain, shoulder) — confirmed out for this match; no fracture but unable to participate.
Victor Munoz (thigh) — doubtful; likely to miss the match.
Austria: David Alaba (minor knee discomfort) — expected to start after precautionary substitution vs Algeria; Rangnick downplayed severity.
Austria: Marko Arnautovic (minor knee knock) — expected to start; scored vs Algeria, came off as precaution only.
No confirmed suspensions for either side heading into this match.
key_factors: Spain's defensive solidity (zero goals conceded in group stage) presents the biggest obstacle for Austria, who failed to score against Argentina.
Austria's Rangnick high-press may paradoxically suit Spain — de la Fuente's side is built to play through pressure with technical midfielders, creating space in behind for Yamal and Baena.
The absences of Nico Williams and Yeremy Pino reduce Spain's directness on the flanks; Alex Baena and Lamine Yamal are expected to carry the width.
Austria accumulated 4 yellow cards in 3 group games (Xaver Schlager led Group J in fouls); aggressive pressing against Spain's skilful ball-carriers could produce more bookings.
Spain averaged approximately 11 corners per group game (34 total) versus Austria's significantly lower output; Spain's territorial dominance in this fixture should push the corner count high.

SoFi Stadium in Inglewood (Los Angeles) is a neutral venue effectively; the indoor/retractable-roof configuration removes weather as a variable. No altitude or heat concerns compared to some other WC venues.
Spain had 4 days' rest after their June 26 final group game; Austria similarly had 4-5 days, so rest differential is negligible.

value_notes: Market-implied probabilities (3-way, overround removed): Spain 72.1%, draw 18.3%, Austria 9.6%. Converting to knockout-stage 2-way by redistributing draw 50/50 gives Spain ~81.3% and Austria ~18.7%. My model places Spain at 76% and Austria at 24%, reflecting modest uncertainty from the Williams/Pino absences that the market may underweight slightly; however, the edge on the h2h market does not reach the 0.05 threshold either way. The clearest value is on BTTS No (market implied ~58.6%, model 72%): edge +0.099 — Spain has conceded zero in the tournament and Austria went scoreless against Argentina; the market appears to be over-indexing on Austria's scoring record against weaker Group J opponents. Totals Under 2.5 (market implied ~50.1%, model 62%): edge +0.094 — Spain's tight defensive structure and only moderate finishing efficiency (5 goals in 3 games, with 4 coming in one blowout) supports under, and Austria's best attacking performances came against Jordan and Algeria. Both BTTS No and Totals Under 2.5 carry model edges above 0.05.
